outcome: frequency of placental abnormalities (maternal vascular malperfusion (MVM) lesions, fetal vascular malperfusion, placental hemorrhage, chronic villitis)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 895 women with singleton gestation who delivered a neonate diagnosed as small-for-gestational age (<10th percentile for gestational age) at a tertiary referral center between 2001 and 2015, and for whom placental pathology was available.
finding: Maternal vascular malperfusion (MVM) pathology significantly decreased in frequency with increasing gestational age, with a notable drop at 33 0/7 weeks, suggesting this gestational age as the optimal cut-off for differentiating early from late fetal growth restriction.
birth_weight: Neonates were defined as small-for-gestational age if birthweight was <10th percentile for gestational age, and severe small-for-gestational age if birthweight was <5th percentile.
gest_age: The study analyzed gestational age at birth, identifying 33 0/7 weeks as a significant cut-off, with subgroups including infants born before and at/after this gestational age.
